summary_paragraph: A woman with a history of primary sclerosing cholangitis, biliary cirrhosis, and celiac disease was admitted with right upper quadrant pain, nausea, and low-grade fever, concerning for recurrent cholangitis. She was started on IV meropenem empirically. An ERCP showed a patent common bile duct with no stones or obstruction. A PICC line was placed for outpatient antibiotic therapy, and she was transitioned to ertapenem. Her symptoms improved, and she was discharged to complete a 14-day course of ertapenem, with plans to restart rifaximin afterward. Chronic conditions including hypothyroidism, hypertension, GERD, depression, and anemia were managed without change. She was stable at discharge with mild residual tenderness and clear mental status.
